boards.title: Your First Weekend at Howard University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A Friday-to-Sunday introduction to Howard through ten distinct, documented campus landmarks and student spaces. Confirm building access and event admission before entering.

cards.title: Begin With Howard’s Art Collection
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Childers Hall
cards.notes: Arrive before the posted 4 p.m. Friday closing, explore the first-floor gallery, and ask ahead if visiting during summer or with a group.
cards.short_summary: Start the weekend inside Howard’s primary visual-arts exhibition space.
cards.evidence_claim: Howard’s Gallery of Art is in Childers Hall at 2455 Sixth Street NW and lists Monday–Friday hours of 10 a.m.–4 p.m.; weekends and major holidays are closed.
cards.source_title: Visit | Chadwick A. Boseman College of Fine Arts
cards.access_notes: Visit Friday between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m. Hours may change; summer visitors and groups should request an appointment. The gallery identifies an accessible front entrance.

cards.title: Learn the Layout From The Yard
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Howard’s central quadrangle
cards.notes: Pause at the quadrangle, identify the surrounding landmarks, and use Founders Library’s tower as your visual anchor for the weekend.
cards.short_summary: Orient yourself where Howard’s major buildings, artworks, and ceremonies converge.
cards.evidence_claim: Howard identifies The Yard as a gathering place bordered by Founders Library, Rankin Chapel, Childers Hall, Douglass Hall, Locke Hall, Carnegie Library, and Blackburn Center.
cards.access_notes: This card covers an outdoor orientation stop only; follow campus notices, event boundaries, and posted restrictions.

cards.title: Find Howard’s Former Main Library
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Southwest side of The Yard
cards.notes: Walk to the exterior from The Yard, read the building in its quadrangle setting, and note its present role in undergraduate support.
cards.short_summary: Connect Howard’s early library history with a building still serving students.
cards.evidence_claim: Opened in 1910, the Carnegie Building served as Howard’s main library until 1939 and now houses Undergraduate Studies and the Office of the Dean of the Chapel.
cards.access_notes: Plan this as an exterior stop unless university business or a scheduled program gives you a reason to enter.

cards.title: Meet Douglass Hall’s Namesake
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · West edge of The Yard
cards.notes: Study the exterior and its relationship to The Yard, then remember this landmark when locating humanities and social-science departments.
cards.short_summary: Add an academic landmark and Frederick Douglass’s Howard connection to your mental map.
cards.evidence_claim: Douglass Hall is a classroom building housing several College of Arts and Sciences departments; Frederick Douglass served on Howard’s Board of Trustees from 1872 to 1895.
cards.access_notes: Use the exterior for this sequence stop; classroom, lounge, and reading-room access depends on current university rules.

cards.title: Locate the Student-Union Hub
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · Blackburn Center
cards.notes: Find Student Life, meeting areas, and dining options now; check the campus calendar before choosing any auditorium or activity space.
cards.short_summary: Learn where many student services, meals, meetings, and campus activities come together.
cards.evidence_claim: Blackburn Center is Howard’s student union and contains Student Life and student-government offices, dining facilities, meeting rooms, lounges, a bowling alley, and event venues.
cards.source_title: Blackburn Center (Armour J. Blackburn University Center) - Howard University
cards.access_notes: Building and venue access may vary with university operations and scheduled events; food and some activities may require payment.

cards.title: Start Saturday at the Clock Tower
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · Founders Library exterior
cards.notes: Circle the exterior, photograph the clock tower from a public campus path, and save interior research questions for verified library hours.
cards.short_summary: Use Howard’s landmark library to connect campus geography with civil-rights history.
cards.evidence_claim: Founders Library is Howard’s main arts-and-sciences library, features five reading rooms and a 167-foot clock tower, and houses the Moorland-Spingarn Research Center.
cards.access_notes: This is a dependable exterior stop. Verify current library hours and eligibility requirements before planning interior access.

cards.title: Trace the Chapel’s Campus Role
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · Beside Founders Library
cards.notes: View the Gothic exterior beside Founders, then consult the chapel calendar if you want to return for a public service or program.
cards.short_summary: Pair a historic worship and speaking venue with the neighboring library landmark.
cards.evidence_claim: Rankin Chapel stands beside Founders Library, is a National Historic Landmark, and contains the sanctuary and Howard Thurman Lounge.
cards.source_title: Rankin Chapel (Andrew Rankin Memorial Chapel) - Howard University
cards.access_notes: Exterior viewing is the planned stop. Enter only for posted services, programs, or other authorized access.

cards.title: Find Howard’s Main Theatre Stage
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · Fine Arts complex
cards.notes: Locate the theater entrance and learn its namesake’s story; attend only when an official performance listing confirms admission details.
cards.short_summary: Recognize the principal performance space for Howard’s Department of Theatre Arts.
cards.evidence_claim: The 300-seat Ira Aldridge Theater is the Department of Theatre Arts’ main performance space and is named for the internationally known Black Shakespearean actor.
cards.source_title: Aldridge Theater (Ira Aldridge Theater) - Howard University
cards.access_notes: No standing public hours are stated. Treat this as an exterior stop unless an official event provides access and ticket information.

cards.title: Check Howard’s Large-Event Venue
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · Sixth Street NW
cards.notes: Compare Cramton’s scale with the nearby Aldridge Theater, then check Howard’s calendar for a future lecture, screening, or performance.
cards.short_summary: Add the campus venue used for major ceremonies, talks, screenings, and shows.
cards.evidence_claim: Cramton Auditorium is a Howard campus venue with more than 1,500 seats that hosts concerts, lectures, screenings, panels, ceremonies, and other events.
cards.access_notes: Interior access and cost depend on the scheduled event. Use the exterior as the default stop and verify official listings before attending.

cards.title: Close With Howard’s Public-TV Legacy
cards.subtitle: Sunday afternoon · Fourth Street NW exterior
cards.notes: Finish at the station exterior and connect the campus to Howard’s public-media work; use WHUT’s official site to explore its programming.
cards.short_summary: End the sequence at Howard’s university-operated public television station.
cards.evidence_claim: Founded in 1980, WHUT is a public television station licensed to and operated by Howard University, with broadcasts reaching the Washington metropolitan region.
cards.access_notes: Plan an exterior stop only; the cited page does not document public tours or general walk-in access.
